title: twoday lost the Danish top spot as Microsoft-centric and too large for a design partner
content:
twoday was the Danish top pick for partnership and is now filed do-not-pitch. The positive finding survives the demotion: it is a proven multi-vendor carrier, top-tier across Microsoft with Databricks, Snowflake and AWS alongside — evidence it can take third-party technology to its clients at scale, which is the behaviour a channel partner has to demonstrate.

Two things overturn it. Being Microsoft-centric means the reference architecture it sells has a strong default gravity toward one vendor's platform, and a client-owned, local-first record layer sits awkwardly against that default. And at 2,200-3,000 people it is too large for a first design partner, which needs a firm where one delivery lead can commit without an alliance review.

The distinction worth carrying is between carrier capability and first-partner suitability. twoday demonstrably has the former, which is why it ranked first in Denmark before the criteria tightened; the current screen asks for the latter, and the two are not the same test. If a second-wave partner programme ever follows the design-partner phase, proven multi-vendor carriers at this scale are the natural cohort to revisit.
